passage: The Mensah group investigated turnover of HIF-1α, a regulatory protein that is rapidly degraded in proliferating cells. To measure stability without confounding new synthesis, cells were treated with cycloheximide, an inhibitor of translation elongation, and harvested at the times shown. Lysates were resolved by SDS-PAGE, transferred to a membrane, and probed with an antibody against HIF-1α; band intensities were quantified and normalized to a loading control. Degradation of HIF-1α was assumed to follow first-order kinetics. The researchers hoped to compare half-lives under normal and stressed conditions and to learn whether proteasome inhibition would stabilize the protein. Results from unstressed cells are shown; each value is the mean of three biological replicates, with errors below 5% of the mean. Equal total protein was loaded in every lane, as confirmed by the loading control. All procedures followed the laboratory's standard operating protocols, and raw data were archived before analysis.

questions.stem: What fraction of HIF-1α remains 60 minutes after cycloheximide treatment?
questions.explanation: At 60 min, two half-lives have elapsed (100 → 50 → 25%).
questions.trap: Stopping at one half-life (50%) or counting three (12.5%); 60 min is two half-lives of 30 min, so 100% falls to 50% and then 25%.

questions.stem: Why is cycloheximide used in this experiment?

options.A: It accelerates proteasomal degradation of all proteins
options.B: It blocks new synthesis so that the loss of existing protein can be followed
options.C: It labels the protein for detection by antibody
options.D: It increases transcription of the gene

questions.explanation: Without blocking translation, newly synthesized protein would obscure the decay of the pre-existing pool.
questions.trap: Thinking cycloheximide speeds degradation or labels the protein; it blocks translation so no new HIF-1α is made and the decay of the existing pool can be followed.

questions.stem: If the decay continues to be first-order, what percentage of HIF-1α remains after 120 minutes?
questions.trap: Miscounting half-lives; 120 min divided by 30 min is 4 half-lives, giving 6.25%, not the value for one more or one fewer half-life.

questions.stem: Which statement about first-order decay is INCORRECT?

options.A: The half-life is independent of starting concentration
options.B: The half-life increases as the starting amount of protein increases
options.C: The half-life equals ln 2 divided by the rate constant
options.D: The rate of decay is proportional to the amount remaining

questions.explanation: In first-order kinetics, t½ = ln 2/k and does not depend on starting concentration.
questions.trap: Choosing a true statement about first-order decay; the half-life is constant (ln 2/k) and does not rise with starting amount, so the claim that it increases is the incorrect one.

questions.stem: HIF-1α turnover is typically controlled by which system?

options.B: Ubiquitination and degradation by the proteasome
options.C: Glycosylation in the Golgi apparatus that prevents degradation
options.D: Phosphorylation by glycolytic kinases that leads to secretion

questions.explanation: Polyubiquitin chains (K48-linked) mark proteins for proteasomal degradation; proteasome inhibitors such as MG132 stabilize short-lived regulatory proteins.
questions.trap: Choosing lysosomal, Golgi or secretion mechanisms because they sound like protein fates; short-lived regulatory proteins such as HIF-1α are ubiquitinated and degraded by the proteasome.
